name: 01-call-and-then-share-context
description: A call a host function hands the machine (Answer::Call) and its then share one context instead of each getting a new empty one

name: 04-handle-reaches-any-run
description: stop/force from a handle reaches whatever run is in progress, not only the run it was taken for

name: 05-force-needs-a-stop-first
description: force from a handle that never stopped anything silently does nothing, so a watchdog that only forces waits for ever

name: 07-park-makes-no-room-to-forget
description: A park doesn't reserve room in the forgotten queue, so dropping a handle needs memory and a refused push loses the only record of the run

name: 08-a-name-out-of-memory-collects
description: An error merely named out-of-memory (host limit) asks for a collection: a name decides something

name: 09-refusal-outside-a-run-no-collection
description: Memory refused outside a run's unwinding (g.string, the reader) asks for no collection, so the host's retry stays refused

name: 10-refusal-collects-at-every-cleanup
description: Out of memory asks for a collection at every cleanup it passes (mark not cleared), so a deep run takes time in the square of its depth

name: 13-a-forged-runner-limit-sets-the-status
description: A program's own (raise (error (quote! broken-pipe))) or forged exit sets the runner's quiet status (the limit flag is not checked)

name: 14-stderr-encoding-hides-stdout-refusal
description: run-process: stderr's catchable encoding-error is raised before stdout's refused memory is seen (can't be put back: run-process no longer reads stderr, G-215)

name: 15-process-output-aborts-when-refused
description: run-process grows its output buffers infallibly, so refused memory aborts the runner

name: 17-closed-stderr-panics
description: The runner's stderr messages use eprint!, which panics when stderr is closed

name: 18-session-lines-restart
description: A terminal session numbers each input's lines from 1, so stdin:N in a trace can't be found

name: 19-printer-bytes-not-charged
description: The printer doesn't count bytes written toward a stop, so a few items that are a lot of text can't be stopped

name: 20-report-printer-depth-unbounded
description: A report's printer stack grows with the data's nesting (no ... past 32 deep), so a small report needs a lot of memory

name: 21-report-counter-restarts-per-value
description: Each value of a report starts a fresh stop counter, so a report of many small values can't be stopped (fixed in be29bf3f)

name: 22-report-checks-not-counted
description: A report's value checks and its search for a place don't count toward a stop

name: 23-report-cuts-names-that-fit
description: A name is cut to its quarter share even when the whole report fits its budget

name: 24-report-ignores-its-budget
description: A report ignores the byte budget the host gives describe, so a report can be megabytes long

name: 25-search-compare-ignores-stop
description: The byte/string search's comparison loop doesn't look for a stop, so a long search can't be stopped (fixed in 83543c23)

name: 25-search-ignores-stop
description: The byte/string search never looks for a stop, in any phase (preparation, skip, comparison), so a long search can't be stopped

name: 26-parameter-walk-ignores-stop
description: match_tree (check_parameters, bind, vau!) doesn't look for a stop, so a walk of a huge shared parameter tree can't be stopped

name: 27-printing-ignores-stop
description: Printing (not reports) never looks for a stop, by item or by byte, so printing a shared tree can't be stopped

name: 28-nested-run-not-refused
description: A run begun inside a host call is not refused (cannot-nest), so nested runs stack on the host's Rust frames

name: 29-reader-strips-every-sign
description: The reader strips all leading signs, so a token with two signs (+-1, --1) is read as a number, not a symbol

name: 30-markdown-tab-beside-run-not-space
description: Markdown: a tab, vertical tab or form feed beside an emphasis run isn't white space

name: 31-markdown-no-multiple-of-three-rule
description: Markdown: runs that can open and close pair even when they make a multiple of three

name: 32-negative-index-countdown
description: A negative list index traverses the list before failing instead of refusing immediately

name: 33-handler-loses-location
description: A handler that fails to be called loses its calling location

name: 34-pad-width-overflows
description: Padding subtracts the input length from a negative extreme width and raises overflow

name: 35-cleanup-swallows-limit
description: A failing cleanup replaces a host limit with its own catchable error

name: 36-binding-names-infallible
description: Listing context bindings allocates infallibly and can abort the host (fixed in 4aba49b0)

name: 37-parse-error-loses-source
description: A named parse error omits the source name

name: 38-retagged-host-value-accepted
description: A host can retag a live reference as a different value kind without rejection

name: 39-host-panic-leaves-run-active
description: A panicking host callback leaves its run active so the interpreter cannot recover

name: 40-last-step-stop-lost
description: A stop during the last host step is ignored when the step returns normally

name: 41-limit-step-stop-lost
description: A pending stop does not replace a limit returned by the final step

name: 42-foreign-owner-not-checked
description: Host values are accepted without checking which interpreter owns them

name: 43-call-allocates-before-collection
description: A call needing argument storage can refuse memory before its first safe point can reclaim garbage

name: 44-handler-values-marked-where-the-error-was
description: A handler's values and trace are marked as library code or not by where the error was raised, not by the combination that set the handler, so a native and its twin trace a caught error's values differently. Retired (G-212): the mark is now an argument of the handler's call, taken from the handler's own frame, so leaving it out doesn't compile and no step's leftover mark exists to read; its patch is gone. Handing the call a constant mark still compiles, and no test catches that

name: 45-long-name-aborts-when-refused
description: The runner hands a path longer than the system takes to Rust's library, whose copy of it aborts when memory is refused

name: 46-new-interpreter-aborts-when-refused
description: Grift::new makes its control block after the heap, so a start with room for only part of the heap aborts
